topics.topic: How cookie-expiry responses avoid deleting a newer session cookie when responses arrive out of order
questions: How can an older response conditionally expire only the session value it received after a concurrent sign-in has already set the same browser cookie to a newer session?
How can a delayed expiry response be prevented from deleting a newer session cookie that the browser installed after the old request arrived?
How must the surface correlate cookie-expiry responses with the session cookie currently installed by the browser when responses arrive out of order?

quotes:
The cookie is expired in the browser in two answers only: to a sign-out
that `owner_sessions.sign_out_owner` accepted, and to a request refused
`unauthenticated` (`no_owner_session`) for the very session its cookie
names. Validity is the one `owner_sessions.admit_owner_request` decided at
arrival; the answer is never re-checked, so it never expires a cookie of a
newer session.
judgement.divergence: A delayed expiry response deletes the shared browser cookie and thereby removes a newer session, or expiry is correlated with the refused session so the newer cookie remains; the owner notices on the next browser request.
judgement.why: The text requires the newer-session guarantee but leaves the owner-interface operation without a mechanism or effect definition that makes expiry conditional on the cookie still holding the refused session.

witness.initial: The browser holds expired session cookie S1, while Registry permits a new concurrent owner session.
events: A browser request carrying S1 is refused `no_owner_session` and its response is delayed.
The owner signs in again, and the browser receives a response setting cookie S2.
The delayed refusal response for S1 reaches the browser after S2 was installed.
outcomes: The expiry response deletes the cookie by its shared name, so S2 is lost.
The expiry is correlated with S1, so S2 remains installed.
witness.observer: The owner, whose next request is either authenticated as S2 or sent without a valid session.
basis:
Several
owner sessions may be open at once; signing in ends none of the others.

names. Validity is the one `owner_sessions.admit_owner_request` decided at
arrival; the answer is never re-checked, so it never expires a cookie of a
newer session.

topics.topic: Refusal precedence in read_import_mapping when import closure and an earlier upload failure both apply
questions: When the import is closed and an uploaded file is also too large, which refusal must `read_import_mapping` return?
When the import is closed and the uploaded file is also invalid at an earlier stage, which refusal must `read_import_mapping` return?

quotes:
**Stages.** An operation that checks stages (3) to (6) of A04 rule 6 checks
them in that order and answers the first failing stage with every failure
of that stage (A04 rule 6).

The closure first: when it exists, refused (A16 rule 8). The file over the
`release_declarations.import_size_limit`, not readable as the format States
5 and 6 declare, holding two projects with one id, or a project without a
readable id or status, refused whole at upload (A16 rule 3, A19 rule 4).
judgement.divergence: The stage-order passage returns `invalid_request` with `file_too_large`, while the closure-first passage returns `refused` with `import_closed`; the owner and owner interface observe the different refusal.
judgement.why: The general State 5 convention orders the stage-(4) size failure before the stage-(6) closure failure, while the import operation explicitly checks the closure first.

topics.topic: Whether confirm_import reports one or all simultaneous stage-six failures
questions: If confirmation finds both an import closure and no kept file, does it report only `import_closed` or every applicable stage-(6) kind?
If the closure exists and the confirmation's bound file is no longer kept, does `confirm_import` return only `import_closed` or every applicable stage-(6) kind?

quotes:
**Stages.** An operation that checks stages (3) to (6) of A04 rule 6 checks
them in that order and answers the first failing stage with every failure
of that stage (A04 rule 6).

The closure first (rule 8); the file of the bound digest still kept, its
digest computed again from the kept bytes (rule 2); the picks checked
again — any conflict, malformed record or missing value, or no pick at all,
refuses the whole import (rule 6); the values the confirmation bound and nothing else;
the projects link to the Customers it makes (R0-80).

`refused` (`import_closed`, `file_not_kept`, `mapping_not_clean`,
`no_picks`).
judgement.divergence: One implementation stops after `import_closed`; another checks all stage-(6) conditions and returns both `import_closed` and `file_not_kept`; the owner interface observes the different refusal kinds.
judgement.why: The operation says to check the closure first but does not say whether that short-circuits the same-stage aggregation required by the general convention.

The second session submits its still-valid confirmation.
outcomes: The operation returns both `import_closed` and `file_not_kept` as simultaneous stage-(6) failures.
witness.observer: The owner using the second session.

topics.topic: How unknown or duplicate project picks are handled and represented by read_import_mapping
questions: How does `read_import_mapping` handle unknown or duplicate project picks, and where are they represented in its answer?

quotes:
The read transaction; the mode, `upload` or `mapping`; the file's bytes;
for `mapping`, the picks — possibly none — each with the display name and
alias it arrives under, and for each Customer the import will make its
name, its kind and whether the v1 value is its tax id.

At `mapping`, the mapping: the picked projects by `project_id`, each one's rooms and
pointers in their lists' orders, the name and alias each arrives under, the
Customers it will make by their v1 value with the projects each links, every
malformed record of the picks, every id of a record the picks bring in that
production already holds — no other production id — and every missing
value; and whether the mapping is clean — no malformed record, no conflict,
no missing value and at least one pick — which alone lets the confirmation
step be shown. A mapping of no pick is not clean (`no_picks`): an import of
nothing is not confirmed.

The file over the
`release_declarations.import_size_limit`, not readable as the format States
5 and 6 declare, holding two projects with one id, or a project without a
readable id or status, refused whole at upload (A16 rule 3, A19 rule 4).
judgement.divergence: An implementation may ignore an unknown pick and coalesce duplicate picks, producing a clean mapping, while another marks the selection invalid or non-clean; the owner observes whether confirmation can proceed and which projects appear.
judgement.why: The mapping operation accepts a collection of picks and defines malformed file records, but does not fix the behaviour for a pick absent from the file or the same project selected more than once.

topics.topic: Required locking and checking order for sessions during an expiry pass
questions: In what order must the pass lock and check owner sessions?

quotes:
Each session that has reached a limit — 8 hours since sign-in or 30
minutes without a request, the reading equal to the limit included — ends,
with its pending confirmation and its uploaded file.

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits, taking the import lock and
then each session's lock and deciding under them, each session by a reading
of `clock.monotonic_reading` taken once its lock is held (A13 rule 2).
judgement.divergence: If session A is visited first, A can remain while B reaches its limit and ends; reversing the visit order can preserve B and end A; the owners using those browser sessions observe which remains authenticated.
judgement.why: Because the operation takes a fresh monotonic reading after acquiring each session lock, its unspecified visitation order can change which sessions expire.

witness.initial: Two owner sessions are just short of their idle limit when an expiry pass begins, and enough time elapses between checks for the second checked session to reach the limit.
events: The pass locks and checks one session, then locks and checks the other with a fresh monotonic reading.
outcomes: Visiting A first preserves A and ends B.
Visiting B first preserves B and ends A.
witness.observer: The owner using the two browser sessions.
basis:
Several
owner sessions may be open at once; signing in ends none of the others.

topics.topic: Whether rendered create-form HTML answers carry request IDs
questions: Are rendered create forms an exception to the convention, so their HTML answers carry request ids?

quotes:
**What answers never carry.** No answer carries a request id: it is kept
with its record and never answered (A01 rule 9). The projections an
operation's Outputs name are complete: a fact not listed there is not in
the answer.

A create form carries a request id from `random_values.mint_identity` made
when it is rendered (A01 rule 1); every form carries the revision or access
version of what it rendered, or none (A04, A12 rule 3); no personal value
or secret in a URL (R0-29); the newest backup's instant on its page (A18
rule 1). Every check is `operations`'.
judgement.divergence: The first passage makes the rendered HTML omit the request id, causing submission to fail as missing, while the second requires the form to carry it so creation can succeed; the owner observes the result.
judgement.why: The convention applies to every public operation answer, including the owner interface's HTML page, but the surface operation explicitly requires that page to carry a generated request id.

topics.topic: Whether sign_out_owner validates absent or invalid sessions itself or relies on admit_owner_request
questions: Can `sign_out_owner` receive and validate an absent or invalid session, or is that refusal produced only by `admit_owner_request` before `sign_out_owner` is called?

quotes:
The admitted session: the step of a sign-out request, which
`admit_owner_request` runs holding the import lock and the session's lock.
`unauthenticated` (`no_owner_session`) when no valid session is named.

The step's answer, or the refusal. For a change the step runs holding the
session's lock — and first the instance's import lock when it reads or
changes an uploaded file — and both are released when the step returns, on
every path (Conventions, "Locks of an owner request").
judgement.why: No admissible flow calls `sign_out_owner` with an absent or invalid session because `admit_owner_request` refuses first, so a witness requires a specified caller that can bypass admission.
